channel.title: Chef Sal Romano — Guides
channel.description: Free guides from Chef Sal Romano: menu tricks, what to order and what to skip, and copycat restaurant dishes you can make at home.

item.title: Homemade Buttermilk Ranch That Beats the Bottle
item.description: Homemade buttermilk ranch like the wing and pizza places serve: fresh herbs, tangy buttermilk, 10 minutes plus a chill. About $1.50 a batch. Free recipe.

item.title: Copycat Cheddar Garlic Biscuits (Like the Seafood Chain's)
item.description: Cheddar garlic biscuits like the seafood chain's basket: why they work, the cold-butter trick, ingredients, mistakes to avoid and what they cost at home.

item.title: Chicken Fajitas, Restaurant Style: The Sizzling Copycat
item.description: Chicken fajitas restaurant style, sizzling at home: why thighs win, the marinade ingredients, the hot-pan trick, common mistakes, and the cost per serving.

item.title: Chicken Parmigiana, Restaurant Style, at Home
item.description: A chicken parmigiana recipe restaurant style: crisp crust, melty mozzarella, sauce on top only. About 45 minutes and roughly $3 a plate at home.

item.title: Copycat Cilantro Lime Rice (Like the Burrito Chain's)
item.description: Copycat cilantro lime rice like the fast-casual burrito chain makes: the bay leaf secret, ingredients, mistakes that make it mushy, and the cost at home.

item.title: Copycat Fettuccine Alfredo: Silky, Not Grainy
item.description: Copycat fettuccine alfredo like the big Italian chain's, made at home in about 20 minutes for roughly $2.50 a plate. The tricks that keep it silky.

item.title: Copycat Breadsticks: Soft, Garlicky, Brushed Twice
item.description: Copycat breadsticks like the bottomless ones at the big Italian chain: soft, buttery and garlicky. About 2 hours, mostly rising, about 25 cents each.

item.title: Loaded Baked Potato Soup: The Restaurant Copycat
item.description: Loaded baked potato soup like the grill chains serve: the mash-half trick, ingredients, mistakes to avoid, toppings, and what a bowl costs at home.

item.title: Copycat Orange Chicken (Crispier Than the Food Court)
item.description: Copycat orange chicken like the mall food court chain: the double-fry trick, ingredients, sauce tips, mistakes that make it soggy, and the cost at home.

item.title: Sausage Potato Kale Soup Like the Italian Chain's
item.description: Creamy sausage potato kale soup like the Tuscan-style bowl at the big Italian chain. About 40 minutes and roughly $2 a bowl when you make it at home.

item.title: Copycat Shrimp Scampi: Tender Shrimp, Bright Sauce
item.description: Copycat shrimp scampi like the Italian and seafood chains make: garlic, butter, white wine and lemon. About 20 minutes and roughly $4 a plate at home.

item.title: Copycat Spinach Artichoke Dip (Restaurant-Style, Hot and Bubbly)
item.description: Copycat spinach artichoke dip like the grill chains serve: why it works, the dry-spinach trick, ingredients, common mistakes, and what it costs at home.

item.title: Restaurant-Style Tiramisu at Home
item.description: Easy tiramisu, restaurant style: no box, no freezer. Mascarpone cream, coffee-dipped ladyfingers, cocoa. About 30 minutes of work, $1.50 a piece.

item.title: White Queso Dip Like the Mexican Restaurants Make
item.description: White queso dip like the Mexican restaurants serve: the deli-cheese secret, ingredients, why queso breaks or turns grainy, and what it costs at home.

item.title: Eating Out vs Cooking at Home: The Real Cost Difference
item.description: Eating out vs cooking at home cost: where your restaurant bill really goes, an example comparison with rounded numbers, and when going out is worth it.

item.title: Garlic Butter Sauce for Steak, Shrimp and Bread
item.description: A 10-minute garlic butter sauce for steak, shrimp, bread and vegetables: butter, garlic, broth, lemon and parsley. About $1.50 a batch. Free recipe.

item.title: How to Save Money Eating Out (Without Eating Sad Food)
item.description: How to save money eating out: a cook's simple plan for drinks, starters, add-ons, specials and dessert, so the bill shrinks but dinner stays a treat.

item.title: How to Tell If Restaurant Food Is Frozen (and Why It Matters)
item.description: How to tell if restaurant food is frozen: the dishes that often arrive frozen, par-baked or in a bag, the clues to watch for, and what to order instead.

item.title: Menu Pricing Tricks Restaurants Use (and How to Spot Them)
item.description: Menu pricing tricks explained: missing dollar signs, prices ending in 9 or round numbers, the decoy dish that anchors you, and why prices don't line up.

item.title: Menu Psychology: How Restaurant Menus Steer Your Order
item.description: Menu psychology explained: where your eye lands first, why some dishes get a box or a photo, and how fancy words nudge you toward what they want sold.

item.title: Restaurant Atmosphere Psychology: Music, Light and Bread
item.description: Restaurant atmosphere psychology: how music, lighting, the salty bread basket, plate size and portions shape how long you stay and how much you order.

item.title: Restaurant Dessert Tricks: Timing, Boxes and Birthday Cake
item.description: Restaurant dessert secrets: why the menu arrives when it does, which desserts often come frozen or from a box, how to ask, and the free birthday dessert.

item.title: Restaurant Drink Markup: Where the Real Money Is
item.description: Restaurant drink markup explained: why soda, coffee, iced tea, wine and cocktails earn more than the food, and simple ways to drink well for less.

item.title: Restaurant Specials and "Market Price": What to Ask First
item.description: Restaurant specials can be the best plate in the house or the fridge clear-out. How to tell the difference, and why you should always ask the market price.

item.title: Restaurant Style Salsa in a Blender (The Free Basket Kind)
item.description: Restaurant style salsa like the free chips-and-salsa basket: why canned tomatoes win, the ingredients, blending mistakes to avoid, and the cost at home.

item.title: Restaurant Upselling Tricks (and How to Tip Fairly)
item.description: Restaurant upselling explained: "Can I start you off with...", the little yeses, side upgrades, and how to tip fairly on the bill you agreed to.

item.title: Smash Burger Recipe Guide: Crispy Edges and Special Sauce
item.description: Smash burger recipe guide: the smash-once trick for crispy lacy edges, ingredients for the burgers and special sauce, common mistakes, and cost at home.

item.title: Homemade Marinara Sauce: Sal's Sunday Marinara
item.description: A homemade marinara sauce that beats the jar: olive oil, onion, garlic, good canned tomatoes and basil. About 45 minutes, about $4 for the whole pot.

item.title: What a Chef Never Orders at a Restaurant
item.description: What chefs never order when they eat out: the well-done steak, Monday fish, the fridge-clearing special, late hollandaise, the pricey plain salad and more.

item.title: The Best Value Dishes at a Restaurant: What a Cook Orders
item.description: The best value dishes at a restaurant, from a cook's point of view: what to order, what to skip, and why the cheapest item is often the best deal.
